info.title: OpenBook REST API
info.description: Experimental first-sprint API for authenticated independent OpenBook applications. Covers instance metadata, current user, persons, posts, post comments and follow relationships, including production installations. Property names and case-sensitive enum values use lowerCamelCase; OAuth protocol fields retain their standard wire names. Creation inputs use separate New<Entity> schemas with independently defined required and nullable fields. Further resources are planned for later sprints.

get.description: RFC 8414 metadata. This is an OAuth 2 authorization server, not an OpenID Connect provider.

Returns general metadata for the OpenBook instance serving this API. The name, description and custom icon reflect the instance settings; domain and base URL identify the configured instance. No usage statistics, contact information, limits or administrative settings are included. Requires an authenticated active account and a Bearer token, even though the metadata is not specific to a user. Uses private caching with ETag and If-None-Match. Authentication and access checks precede HTTP 304. Last-Modified is not emitted.

get.description: Returns a direct array of PersonReference objects for available people with a pending request to follow the authenticated user. Accepted, rejected and withdrawn requests are excluded. Requests addressed to community identities or other accounts are not included, regardless of staff roles. Reads only the state known by this instance; no remote fetch is performed. Supports after, limit (default 20, maximum 100), sort=personId and direction=asc or desc. cursor and page are not supported. Authentication and availability checks precede conditional responses.

get.summary: List posts published by the authenticated user
get.description: Returns a direct array of Post objects authored by the authenticated user. Only published posts are included; deleted posts and private conversation messages are excluded. Includes the user's own restricted posts, community posts and quotes. Announces of other authors' posts are excluded. An authored post that has also been announced appears once in publication order, without postAnnounce or postTimelineAt. Uses newest-first publication order, with postId as the tie-breaker. Supports after, limit, sort and direction. engine, afterAt, cursor and page are not supported. No remote content is fetched. Requires an active authenticated account. Conditional requests are evaluated after authentication and current account checks.

get.description: Returns the person identified by personId. Requires an authenticated active account with a Bearer token. Local and remote accounts use the same Person representation. Locally suspended profiles are not available in this initial version. Conditional requests are evaluated only after authentication, remote refresh and availability checks. get.summary: Get your follow state towards a person
get.description: Returns the authenticated user's outgoing Follow state towards this person. An available person with no outgoing follow returns 200 with followStatus=none, not 404. Reads the state currently known by this instance without fetching remote profiles or retrying follow requests. Local open accounts are normally accepted immediately; protected local accounts require approval. Remote non-feed identities remain pending until acceptance is received. A rejected or withdrawn request returns to none. The reverse relationship is not included. The current user's own relation can be read even for a private community identity; other members are not disclosed. Requires an authenticated active account. Authentication and availability checks precede conditional responses.

put.summary: Follow a person or request approval
put.description: Creates or maintains the authenticated user's outgoing follow. No request body is required; the acting identity comes only from the Bearer token. Returns Follow with the resulting state: accepted for open local accounts and feeds, pending for protected local accounts and remote non-feed identities until acceptance arrives. Repeated requests reuse the relationship, but pending remote requests may be sent again. A pending local request may become accepted if the target has opened their account. Self-follow and inactive target accounts are refused with 422. New follows of remotely suspended identities return 403. Community identities follow their membership permissions, including the owner's membership protection. No response caching. Requires an authenticated active account.

get.summary: List a person's posts and announces
get.description: Returns a direct array of Post objects matching the Posts tab of the specified profile: authored posts and selected announces, filtered by the authenticated user's visibility. Recent remote content is imported when due under the existing cache policy; unavailable remote servers fall back to locally available content. RSS/Atom profiles follow the configured feed refresh interval. Results are a partial local view, not a complete remote archive. The person detail operation does not perform this content import. Each entry includes postTimelineAt for ordering and, when applicable, postAnnounce identifying the profile's announce. Ordinary profiles order by the selected announce or publication time; groups use original publication time. The page size follows the website feed configuration and cannot be selected per request. Follow the next Link using after plus afterAt. limit, cursor, page and engine are not accepted. Revalidation is performed after refresh, availability and access checks. Local private community walls require membership or ownership. Requires an authenticated active account and a Bearer token.

parameters.name: personId
parameters.description: The person identifier within this OpenBook instance.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The postId of the last entry on the previous page. Required together with afterAt. The reference need not remain available. Follow the next Link.

parameters.name: afterAt

404.description: The post or comment is missing, deleted, inaccessible, belongs to another post, or is a private conversation message. Writes also require ownership of the comment.

example.title: Not Found
example.detail: The person was not found or is not available through this endpoint.

Person.description: A user-facing identity representing an individual, a software application, a feed or a group. Local and remote identities use the same representation. A group Person represents the community identity; the Community resource represents its space and features. Deleted identities are not returned as Person resources; requests for their details return HTTP 404.

personId.description: The person identifier within the OpenBook instance.

personUri.description: The canonical ActivityPub identifier of the person.

personType.description: The kind of identity: person for an individual, application for software, feed for a feed source, or group for a community identity. Values are case-sensitive. Account roles are described separately.

personDomain.description: The domain of the account identity.

personStatus.description: The effective account status: active for an active account, inactive for a blocked, disabled or suspended account. Local and remote accounts use the same values. An active status does not grant access to every operation. Values are case-sensitive.

personPublishedAt.description: The creation or publication date associated with this identity. For local user accounts this is the OpenBook registration date; for other identities it is the date available from their profile. Null when unavailable.

personProfile.description: The public profile of a person.

personName.description: The display name. The username is used when no display name is available.

personSummary.description: The biography or description as source text, without HTML rendering by the API. It may contain Markdown; clients are responsible for rendering it. For remote accounts this is the text available to OpenBook, not necessarily the original content from the origin server. The property may be omitted or null when unavailable; an empty string is allowed.

personAvatar.description: The avatar image URL, or null when unavailable.

personCoverImage.description: The cover image URL, or null when unavailable.

personFields.description: Additional profile fields in display order. Empty when no fields are available.

items.description: An additional profile field containing text or a URL.

label.description: The display label of the field.

value.description: The field value. It may be plain text or a URL.

personDiscoverable.description: Whether the person allows inclusion in account suggestions.

personIndexable.description: Whether the person allows indexing of their public content.

personFollowApproval.description: Whether following this person requires approval.

personCustomEmojis.description: Custom emoji shortcodes mapped to image URLs. An empty object indicates no custom emojis.

additionalProperties.description: The image URL for this shortcode.

personAlsoKnownAs.description: Declared aliases of the person. Empty when no aliases are available.

personMovedTo.description: A reference to the account migration destination. May be omitted or null when no destination is declared.

personId.description: The person identifier within the OpenBook instance.

personUri.description: The canonical ActivityPub identifier of the person.

personMemorial.description: Whether this is a memorial account.

personSuspended.description: Whether the person is suspended. The same meaning applies to local and remote accounts. A suspended account always has personStatus inactive; an inactive account is not necessarily suspended.

personFollowersCount.description: The follower count displayed by OpenBook, when included. Null when unavailable; zero means a known count of zero.

personFollowingCount.description: The following count displayed by OpenBook, when included. Null when unavailable; zero means a known count of zero.

personRoles.description: Descriptive account roles: admin or moderator. An account may have both roles. An empty array indicates neither role; the property may be omitted when role information is unavailable. These values do not grant administrative or moderation access through the API.

PersonReference.description: A compact Person reference for lists and related resources. The same representation is used for individuals, applications, feeds and groups.

personId.description: The person identifier within this OpenBook instance.

personUsername.description: The account username without the domain.

personName.description: The display name, falling back to the username when no display name is available.

personAvatar.description: The avatar image URL. Omitted when no avatar is available.

Me.description: The current authenticated user context. Its properties use the my prefix. The initial representation contains only the authenticated person.

myPerson.description: The authenticated account, using the full Person representation.

Location.description: A geographic place reusable across resources.

Media.description: The media information included in a post attachment.

mediaUrl.description: The absolute URL of the media.

mediaPreviewUrl.description: The preview URL provided by OpenBook; it may equal mediaUrl.

mediaMimeType.description: The MIME type of the media.

Post.description: A post returned by an authenticated feed. This initial representation includes text, author, warning, media, location, counters and current-user interactions. Polls, quotes and other related resources are not yet represented.

postId.description: The post identifier within this instance.

postUri.description: The canonical identifier of the post.

postName.description: The post title, omitted when empty.

postContent.description: The textual content available to OpenBook. It may contain Markdown syntax and is not rendered to HTML by this API. It may be empty for media-only posts.

postCW.description: Whether OpenBook applies a content warning to the post.

postCWText.description: The effective warning text, when available.

postVisibility.description: The audience of the post. This does not grant access to private messages.

postSourceUri.description: The original source identifier or article link, omitted when empty.

postCustomEmojis.description: Emoji names mapped to image URLs; omitted when empty.

postAttachments.description: Attached media in presentation order. Omitted when empty.

postLocation.description: The associated place, or null when none is available.

postMyInteractions.description: Interactions performed by the authenticated user. A direct announce means a manual share.

postTimelineAt.description: Present in timeline and person-post list responses. The timestamp used to order this entry: the selected announce time or original publication time, except that group profiles always use original publication time. Use this value as afterAt when continuing from this post.

postAnnounce.description: Optional announce context for a Post. Present when the feed entry has a selected announce; omitted otherwise. The home timeline uses the latest relevant announce by the user or a followed account. A person-post list uses the profile's selected announce. Describes one announce, not all shares of the post. World and post details do not select an announce context. An author may announce their own post. Original authorship remains in postAuthor.

announcePublishedAt.description: Publication date of the selected announce.

NewPost.description: Input for creating a text post. Uses the same property names as Post, with independent input requirements. The author is determined by the authenticated account. Only postContent and postVisibility are required; future additional creation fields will be optional.

postContent.description: The post text, which may contain Markdown, hashtags and mentions. Must contain non-whitespace text and respect the instance's configured post length limit.

postVisibility.description: The audience of the new post. Must be provided explicitly. Direct posts are not supported by this initial creation schema.

PatchPost.description: Partial input for editing a simple post. Each property is optional, but at least one must be provided. Omitted properties retain their values; null values are not accepted.

postContent.description: The post text, which may contain Markdown, hashtags and mentions. Must contain non-whitespace text and respect the instance's configured post length limit.

postVisibility.description: The new audience of the post. Omit this property to preserve the current audience.

Instance.description: General metadata of the current OpenBook instance. Contains no usage statistics or administrative configuration.

instanceName.description: The configured display name of the instance.

instanceDomain.description: The configured instance domain used for federated addresses.

instanceUrl.description: The configured absolute base URL of the instance, without a trailing slash.

instanceDescription.description: The configured instance description, without additional rendering. An empty string when no description is configured.

instanceIcon.description: Absolute URL of the configured custom 512-pixel PNG icon. Omitted when no custom icon is configured.

Follow.description: The authenticated user's outgoing follow state towards the person identified in the request path. This does not describe the reverse relationship.

followStatus.description: none: not followed and no request is pending. pending: awaiting acceptance. accepted: currently followed. Rejected or withdrawn requests return to none.

PatchFollowRequest.description: Accepts a pending request addressed to the authenticated user.

ProblemDetails.description: Problem Details as defined by RFC 9457.

type.description: The URI identifying the problem type.

title.description: A short description of the problem type.

status.description: The HTTP status code of this response.

detail.description: An explanation specific to this occurrence.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence, when available.

code.description: A machine-readable reason when available. Creating a post before email verification returns emailVerificationRequired.

QueryValidationProblemDetails.description: Problem Details as defined by RFC 9457.

type.description: The URI identifying the problem type.

title.description: A short description of the problem type.

status.description: The HTTP status code of this response.

detail.description: An explanation specific to this occurrence.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence, when available.

errors.description: Validation messages keyed by query parameter.

BodyValidationProblemDetails.description: Problem Details as defined by RFC 9457.

type.description: The URI identifying the problem type.

title.description: A short description of the problem type.

status.description: The HTTP status code of this response.

detail.description: An explanation specific to this occurrence.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence, when available.

errors.description: Validation messages keyed by request property, or body for an invalid top-level JSON value.

Comment.description: A published comment or nested reply belonging to a post visible to the authenticated user. Comments inherit the post audience. Deleted comments are not returned; their published replies remain available.

commentId.description: The comment identifier within this instance.

commentPostId.description: The root post identifier within this instance.

commentParentId.description: The parent comment identifier, or null for a reply to the post. A parent may have been deleted and no longer be retrievable.

commentContent.description: The text available to OpenBook, without additional HTML rendering. It may contain Markdown or plain text; the original remote document is not guaranteed.

commentEditedAt.description: The latest known edit time. Omitted when no edit is known.

commentLanguage.description: The declared language when available; omitted when absent.

commentCustomEmojis.description: Custom emoji shortcodes mapped to image URLs. Omitted when empty.

commentAttachments.description: Existing attachments in display order. Omitted when empty.

commentCounters.description: Counts known to this instance; federated counts may be incomplete.

commentLiked.description: Whether the authenticated user likes this comment.

example.commentContent: Thank you for sharing this walk.

NewComment.description: Inputs for a new text comment. Only commentContent is required. Author and audience follow the authenticated user and target post. Future creation fields will be optional.

commentContent.description: Non-whitespace comment text. Markdown and mentions are supported. Must respect the instance’s configured comment length limit.

commentParentId.description: Optional parent comment in the same post. Omit or use null for a top-level comment. The parent must still be published.

example.commentContent: Thank you for sharing this walk.

PatchComment.description: Edit the text of an owned local published comment. Existing attachments and reply relationships are preserved.

commentContent.description: Non-whitespace comment text. Markdown and mentions are supported. Must respect the instance’s configured comment length limit.

openBookOAuth.description: User authorization using Authorization Code with PKCE S256. Register the application and its redirect URI with the instance. Public clients do not use a client secret. Access tokens are long-lived JWT Bearer credentials with server-side revocation checks. Account availability is checked on every request. The default token lifetime is 365 days and may vary by instance. Refresh tokens allow renewal without another browser login.

servers.description: The REST API of this OpenBook instance.
